concepts.name: Repository and object model
concepts.description: Commits, trees and blobs in a content-addressed store — everything else in git is a view over this.

concepts.name: Commits
concepts.description: An immutable snapshot plus parent pointers; history is a DAG, not a list.

concepts.name: Staging area
concepts.description: The index — the explicit space between working tree and commit that makes partial commits possible.

concepts.name: Branches
concepts.description: A movable pointer to a commit; branching is cheap because nothing is copied.

concepts.name: Remotes and tracking branches
concepts.description: Local mirrors of another repository's refs, updated only by fetch.

concepts.name: .gitignore
concepts.description: Patterns excluding files from tracking — and why it does nothing for already-tracked files.

concepts.name: Merging
concepts.description: Joining histories with a merge commit; fast-forward versus true merge.

concepts.name: Rebasing
concepts.description: Replaying commits onto a new base, producing new commit objects with new hashes.

concepts.name: Conflict resolution
concepts.description: What a conflict actually is, and why resolving it is a content decision git cannot make.

concepts.name: Stashing
concepts.description: Parking uncommitted work on a hidden ref to get a clean tree.

concepts.name: Detached HEAD
concepts.description: HEAD pointing at a commit rather than a branch, and how commits made there get orphaned.

concepts.name: Git hooks
concepts.description: Local scripts fired at lifecycle points such as pre-commit — the mechanism Eklavya's own gate uses.

concepts.name: reset --soft/--mixed/--hard
concepts.description: Which of HEAD, index and working tree each mode moves — the difference between recoverable and lost work.

concepts.name: Reflog
concepts.description: The local log of where refs have pointed; the recovery tool for almost every 'I lost it' situation.

concepts.name: Cherry-picking
concepts.description: Applying one commit's change onto another branch, and the duplicate-commit problem it creates.

concepts.name: Merge vs rebase: tradeoffs
concepts.description: Truthful history versus readable history, and why the choice is a team policy, not a technical fact.

concepts.name: Interactive rebase
concepts.description: Reordering, squashing and editing history — and what it does to anyone who already pulled it.

concepts.name: Force-push safety
concepts.description: Why --force-with-lease exists and what plain --force silently destroys.

concepts.name: Bisect
concepts.description: Binary search over history to find the commit that introduced a regression.
